review_comments.body: this changes the capture semantics substantially, I'd rather prefer we fix this for the rails specific issue.

### Causes marked when capture fails **Medium Severity** `mark_causes_as_captured` runs in `tap` even when `capture_exception` returns no event. An excluded wrapper still marks its causes, so a later `ErrorSubscriber` report of a non-excluded cause is treated as already captured and dropped.
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit a240ac1350ee328d328bccc7c9ca088ace6ba86d. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

comments.body:
Thanks, agreed. I reverted the core change (`Hub#capture_exception` and `Sentry.exception_captured?` are back to their original semantics) and moved the fix into `Sentry::Rails::CaptureExceptions`: it marks the causes of the exception it captured, so `ErrorSubscriber` doesn't report them again, and it skips an exception whose cause was already reported through the error reporter (the development order). Specs in `sentry-rails/spec/sentry/rails/capture_exceptions_spec.rb` cover both orders and an unrelated exception.


This comment was drafted with Claude Code.

Good catch, Bugbot was right: `mark_causes_as_captured` ran inside `tap` even when `capture_exception` returned no event, so an excluded wrapper (`excluded_exceptions`) marked its causes and a later `ErrorSubscriber` report of a non-excluded cause was dropped. In b0fe83b the causes are marked only when an event was actually sent, and a spec covers the excluded-wrapper case (it failed before the change).

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.
